name: Nissa's Remains
summary: Nissa's remains belong to a noblewoman of the once-wealthy Agamand dynasty in northern Tirisfal Glades. Slain and made mindless servants of the Scourge during the Third War, Nissa and her family are now hunted by former laborers seeking vengeance.

sections.title: A Legacy of Pride
sections.body: Before the Third War, the Agamands were Tirisfal Glades' wealthiest and most influential dynasty. Their prosperous mills stood across the northern hills. When the Plague of Undeath spread through Lordaeron, the family patriarchs refused to flee. They fortified their estates and persuaded their retainers and laborers to stay and fight. Their pride cost them their lives. The Scourge slew the Agamands, then raised them as mindless thralls bound to the Lich King's will.

sections.title: Bitter Retribution
sections.body: In Brill, survivors who later broke free under Queen Sylvanas Windrunner still remember the Agamands' fatal pride. Coleman Farthing, once a laborer in their mills, resents his former masters for luring the workers into undeath. He charges adventurers with putting down the risen Agamands and retrieving their physical remains, including Nissa's. For Farthing and other Forsaken, destroying these relics offers a grim sense of closure and revenge.

faq.answer: Nissa Agamand belonged to the noble Agamand family, which owned the sprawling Agamand Mills in Tirisfal Glades. When the Scourge swept through Lordaeron, she died with her kin and was raised as an undead minion under the Lich King's control.

faq.q: Why does Coleman Farthing want Nissa's remains?
faq.answer: Coleman Farthing worked in the Agamand mills while alive. He resents the family for refusing to flee and persuading their loyal workers to stay behind and die. Gathering the family's remains lets him take revenge on his former masters.
Nissa Agamand haunts the ruined Agamand Mills in northern Tirisfal Glades. She wanders among the decrepit farmhouses with her reanimated relatives and mindless Scourge thralls.

faq.q: Did Nissa retain her free will like the Forsaken?
faq.answer: No. Nissa and her family remained enslaved to the Scourge as mindless undead, unlike the Forsaken who broke free from the Lich King. They lacked the sentience and freedom of Undercity's citizens.

angles.text: For the Forsaken, reclaiming Tirisfal means purging their former Scourge oppressors and the wealthy aristocrats whose foolish pride doomed common laborers to undeath.
Slaying the reanimated Agamands and clearing their mills helps secure northern Tirisfal Glades from Scourge pockets that threaten Brill and the Undercity.
